title: Murmuration: Chromatic Chorus
team: Myeongseong Kim, Ahyeon Lee, Joo-Hong Shin, Gaeun Kang, NaYeon Lee, Bora Youn, Donghyeon Son
summary: A multi-user XR installation that transforms hand-folded and personalized paper birds into virtual agents.
Participants encounter these birds together in a shared immersive environment, forming a collective experience.

paragraph: Murmuration: Chromatic Chorus is a participatory XR installation where hand-crafted paper birds become persistent virtual agents.
Visitors fold and decorate a paper bird, then record a short vocal gesture.

Carrying each participant’s colors, patterns, and voice, the bird crosses into XR as a living trace of its maker, joining a shared virtual flock where individual marks become flight, sound, and relational trails.

The work investigates how physical traces become virtual presences, how non-living artifacts acquire agency and relational meaning, how participants perceive and connect with these entities, and how their encounters accumulate into collective movement, social connection, and shared memory.
Inside the multi-user XR space, each bird flies among birds created by current and previous visitors, leaving a thread-like trail drawn from the main color of its paper body.
These lingering trails cross and layer in the air, gradually stitching the space into a chromatic fabric of flight.
When a bird touches another trace, it releases its call, turning accidental collisions into fragments of an unpredictable chorus.

In this sense, Chromatic Chorus refers both to the visual and sonic composition of colored trails and bird calls, and to a plural harmony in which distinct participant-made beings keep their individuality while resonating with others.
The birds do not disappear after a single visit.
They remain in the virtual world, continuing to move, sound, and shape future encounters as part of an evolving ecology.
New visitors therefore enter a space already inhabited by others’ colors, voices, flights, and collisions, adding their own bird to a growing field of traces.
Through these accumulated encounters, participants become connected not only to those sharing the space in the present, but also to those who have already left it.
Murmuration: Chromatic Chorus explores how XR can weave physical traces into virtual presence, presence into relation, and relation into a living ecology of collective memory.
